newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Cricket-South Africa crush India by 328 runs.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-South Africa crush India by 328 runs.

text.p: Superb fast bowling from Allan Donald paved the way for a comprehensive South African victory over India, who made just 66 in their second innings in the first test at Kingsmead on Saturday.
South Africa won by 328 runs after Donald, who took five for 40 in India's first innings, rocked the Indian top order on the third day with a hostile opening spell of three for 10 in six overs.

Generating extreme pace on a pitch still offering plenty of bounce, the 30-year-old finished with second innings figures of four for 14 as India were bowled out for a meagre 66 in 34.1 overs - their joint fourth-lowest test total.
Donald was well supported by new ball partner Shaun Pollock, who took three for 25, and Lance Klusener, who returned figures of two for 16.
In front of a third day crowd of 13,500 in hot and humid conmditions, South Africa drew first blood in the three-match series with more than two days to spare.

India's number six batsman Rahul Dravid, batting confidently for an unbeaten 27 in two hours, at least ensured that India surpassed their lowest ever test total of 42 all out - achieved against England at Lord's in 1974.
Earlier, India had been set an improbable victory target of 395 after South Africa were bowled out for 259 in their second innings shortly before lunch.
All-rounder Brian McMillan finished on 51 not out and seamer Venkatesh Prasad took five for 93 for match figures of 10 for 153 - his first 10-wicket haul at test level.
Yet the third morning began disastrously for the home side as they lost five wickets for the further addition of just 21 runs.
Prasad and fellow strike bowler Javagal Srinath achieved movement off the seam and, helped by some loose South African batting, they reduced the home side to 185 for nine.
But McMillan frustrated the buoyant Indian attack with a muscular 51 not out as South Africa eventually opened up their substantial lead.
McMillan and Donald, who made 26, shared in a 10th-wicket stand of 74 to frustrate the Indian attack for 11 overs.

Donald then rocked the Indian top order with his fiery opening burst to leave them reeling at seven for three. From that point, there was no way back for an Indian side lacking the necessary application.
"On our side, it was a case of bad batting - we should have applied ourselves a lot more and showed more determination," Indian captain Sachin Tendulkar, who made just four, said.
"But I think it was basically a bowlers' wicket, although batting did get better if the batsmen stayed there for a while without taking any risks."
South African captain Hansie Cronje was in agreement: "It was never easy to bat on this wicket because of the steep bounce - you were never really quite set as a batsman.

"What also helped us was that we had four players who have a sound back-foot technique in Andrew Hudson, Adam Bacher, Brian McMillan and Shaun Pollock. And the partnership between Hudson and Bacher on the first morning, which took us to 70 for one, was the turning point in the game for me."

"I think we also had a slight advantage with our four fast bowlers compared to their two. If Allan Donald and Shaun Pollock needed a rest, we always had Lance Klusener and Brian McMillan to bring on."
South Africa second innings (overnight 164 for four)
Bowling: Srinath 23-5-80-3 (1-nb), Prasad 25-4-93-5 (2-nb), Johnson 9-1-39-0 (2-nb), Kumble 11-3-26-2, Ganguly 2-0-8-0.
Result: South Africa won by 328 runs.
